summary: Pre-trip intro post: Rebecca introduces herself and the eight-member 2024 team, who are route planning, fundraising, and setting up learning festivals before the summer ride.
planning_notes: Donations go through giving.mit.edu/search/node/spokes; check giving.mit.edu/matching-gifts first to see whether the donor's employer matches gifts.
Team trained with indoor and long outdoor rides and considered the Boston Midnight Marathon ride as a training/fundraising event.

summary: Team members recount their spring break trips: a lithium policy research trip in Arkansas, a yurt stay in Vermont, a Finger Lakes AirBnB, a Peru trek, a Montreal trip, a Natchez Trace ride in Mississippi, and a Saranac Lake stay.
planning_notes: Northeast spring weather is unreliable: a Montreal-bound bike ride was derailed by a snowstorm, and Vermont saw 20+ inches of snow in early spring.
Natchez Trace Parkway (Natchez to Clinton/Port Gibson, MS) was ridden by one member as a scenic day ride.

summary: Days -1 and 0 were spent driving and prepping near DC. Day 1 was the first learning festival, split between the DC Jail (adults over 18) and the DC Youth Services Center, teaching concrete chemistry (Krispie Koncrete), strawberry DNA, a 3D-printed boat, and Scratch coding.
slept_at: Heather and Maurice's home, northern Virginia (Oakton area) (host)
learning_festival: DC Department of Corrections (DC Jail, adults over 18) and DC Youth Services Center (juvenile students, most under 16); coordinated by Judge Faruqui's team. Activities: Krispie Koncrete (concrete chemistry), strawberry DNA extraction with household soap, 3D-printed boat demo, Scratch intro. Activities were built into students' school days, so teachers and administrators were involved.
contacts: Heather and Maurice (hosts, northern Virginia / DC area)
Judge Faruqui and team (DC, coordinated learning festivals at DC Jail and YSC)
planning_notes: Learning festivals in DC ran inside students' school days, so coordinate with teachers and administrators in advance.
A 3D printer and demo boat could be shuttled between classrooms for hands-on demos.
Small juvenile-facility class sizes let teams learn student names and do one-on-one engagement.

summary: First riding day, Oakton VA to Linden VA: several falls (Hank, Jess on a gravel road), a bike breakdown that needed a van pickup, and the discovery that the rental minivan had bald front tires, which forced a rest day.
slept_at: Jen and Tim's home, Linden VA (host; stayed two nights)
contacts: Jen and Tim (hosts, Linden VA; provided vegan meal options and tacos)
Heather (host, Oakton VA)
planning_notes: Inspect rental cars before leaving: the team's rental had bald front tires, and Avis staff said renters could not open the hood to inspect.

Discontinued Garmin Edge units bought online may have the Europe cycling map and no room for North America maps; buy the correct model from a local bike shop (REI/bike shops near Oakton were mapped for this).
Gravel driveways to hosts can cause falls; ride them slowly or walk them.

summary: Rest day in Linden VA: two riders tried to get a new rental car at Dulles after the bald-tire discovery, which took three rentals and an Uber ride. The team also got bikes checked and fitted in Winchester VA and cooked dinner together.
slept_at: Jen and Tim's home, Linden VA (host)
contacts: Jen and Tim (hosts, Linden VA)
planning_notes: Dulles-area Avis: a miscommunication sent riders to Springfield VA, 45 minutes from Dulles; allow extra time and confirm the pickup location.
Avis does not allow renters to open the hood or inspect the engine in the lot; the team drove to a nearby shopping-mall lot to inspect the third rental.
Winchester VA has a bike shop that checked and fitted bikes on a rest day (shop name not stated).

summary: Shenandoah National Park (Big Meadows camp) to Waynesboro VA: a fast downhill out of the park, lunch at Lil Gus's in Grottoes, then a long detour to add all riders as authorized drivers on the rental car at an Avis 45 minutes away, where only four additional drivers could be added.
slept_at: Francine's home, Waynesboro VA (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Francine (Warmshowers host, Waynesboro VA)
Lil Gus's (restaurant, Grottoes VA; friendly waitstaff, good lunch stop)
planning_notes: Get every rider added as an authorized driver on the rental before the trip starts; Avis would only add four extra people on the day, and only the primary driver can authorize changes.
Shenandoah NP to Waynesboro is a fast downhill out of the park, then farm backroads with many rolling hills.
Lil Gus's in Grottoes VA is a good lunch stop after a hot climb.

summary: Note: this file is the Day 4 post (title and date say Day 4 and 2024-06-10; the filename says day-6). Linden VA to Shenandoah NP: a 60.9-mile, 7,569 ft day where the support van's hybrid rental failed on Skyline Drive, leaving the support crew stranded for hours until a tow, a replacement rental, and a truck to move camping gear were arranged. Riders reached Big Meadows Campground after dark.
slept_at: Big Meadows Campground, Shenandoah NP (camping). Support crew slept at Heather's home near Dulles after a 1am rental pickup.
contacts: Blue Ridge Bicycles, VA (fixed a bent derailleur)
Jason (tow truck driver, Front Royal / Dulles area)
Sandi and Chris (Edgerton Center advisors, MIT; helped arrange the replacement rental)
Tim (drove shuttle to the trailhead)
Heather (host, DC area)
planning_notes: Only the primary driver on a company rental can authorize swaps and tows, so the primary driver must be present or reachable; add all riders as authorized drivers before leaving.
Keep the support vehicle and camping gear with the riding group or within reach; the team had no camp gear for the night after the van broke down.
Skyline Drive has an Appalachian Trail resupply point that sells MREs and soft serve.
Front Royal VA: a Taco Bell parking lot was used as a waiting spot during a two-hour tow wait; the hybrid Chrysler Pacifica rental had an electrical fault that needed a mechanic's reset.

summary: Flat ride from Waynesboro to Lexington VA (43.8 mi), where riders reflected on adjusting to 8-hour riding days, then spent the afternoon kayaking and paddleboarding with Warmshowers hosts Dirk and Chrissy.
slept_at: Dirk and Chrissy's home, Lexington VA (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Dirk and Chrissy (Warmshowers hosts, Lexington VA; kayak/paddleboard on the river, dinner)
planning_notes: Expect saddle soreness and leg lactic build-up in the first week of 8-hour riding days.
Dirk and Chrissy's Lexington VA home is a strong Warmshowers stop: river access for paddling and a host who gave bike fitting advice.

summary: Lexington to Roanoke VA (58.6 mi): a water stop on Plank Road, lunch at a Buchanan picnic area, a closed bike path detoured onto a highway for 20 miles, and a Roanoke bridge demolition that forced a detour before reaching hosts Howard and Lynn.
slept_at: Howard and Lynn's home, Roanoke VA (host)
contacts: Howard and Lynn (hosts, Roanoke VA; had read the team's website)
Dirk (Lexington VA host; gave bike fitting advice before departure)
planning_notes: Bike path closed near Buchanan VA for cliff maintenance / falling-rock risk; the team took the highway instead for about 20 miles.
Roanoke has road closures from a bridge demolition; navigation can send you across town, so check current closures.
Buchanan VA picnic area has very clean porta-potties and is a good lunch stop.

summary: Tazewell VA to Breaks Interstate Park (70.9 mi, 5,851 ft): a flat on Cleo's tire that could not be fixed roadside because the team had no pump and the tire was not actually tubeless; the van had to return to help, and the team camped at the VA/KY border.
slept_at: Breaks Interstate Park campground, VA/KY border (camping)
planning_notes: Carry a pump and a spare tube or plugs on every ride; the team had no pump and had to call the van.
Check whether a tire is truly tubeless before plugging it; a bacon-strip plug failed because the tire had three holes and was not tubeless.
Hills in SW Virginia reach 13% grade with hairpin descents; brake carefully.

summary: Rest day at Breaks Interstate Park: the team napped in hammocks, one rider got a flat fixed at a local bike shop while the car was used, and the group ate at the Rhododendron Restaurant. Tents in the open field got very hot by morning.
slept_at: Breaks Interstate Park campground (camping; tents in open field)
contacts: Rhododendron Restaurant, Breaks Interstate Park (lunch)
planning_notes: Breaks Interstate Park campground tents sit in an open field and become ovens by mid-morning; get shaded sites or leave early.
Local bike shop repaired a flat the day before; check nearby shop hours on rest days.

summary: Draper VA to Tazewell VA (69.1 mi, 4,701 ft): a rider pushed through shin-splint pain on the team's longest ride so far, with a steep downhill in the first 25 miles and a night at Main Street Methodist Church in Tazewell.
slept_at: Main Street Methodist Church, Tazewell VA (church host)
contacts: Theresa, Main Street Methodist Church, Tazewell VA (host; invited team to a recovery program meeting)
planning_notes: A steep downhill in the first 25 miles out of Draper VA has signs telling trucks to downshift; riders braked hard on sharp curves.
Compression sleeves and calf socks plus Icy Hot helped with shin splints on a 70-mile day.
Main Street Methodist Church in Tazewell VA hosted the team with meals and welcomed them to a community meeting.

summary: Roanoke VA to Draper VA (60.9 mi): after closed routes forced a reroute, the team lunched in Christiansburg and reached a Warmshowers winery property in Draper, where they toured the vines and ate pizza outside.
slept_at: Curtis and Jenny's home, Draper VA (Warmshowers host, winery property)
contacts: Curtis and Jenny (Warmshowers hosts, Draper VA)
Howard and Lynn (hosts, Roanoke VA; breakfast before departure)
planning_notes: Route from Roanoke to Draper roughly followed the TransAmerica Bicycle Trail on back roads; closed routes forced a reroute, so check closures before leaving.
Check for ticks after time in grass at the Draper winery property (one rider picked one up).

summary: Breaks Interstate Park to Hazard KY (77.9 mi, 4,255 ft): the team was chased by dogs, including one that caused a crash into bushes, and rode past a coal-history mural and a dairy bar before reaching a Hazard B&B.
slept_at: Bed & Breakfast in Hazard KY (host Sherry)
contacts: Sherry (B&B host, Hazard KY; ordered pizza for the team)
Hemphill Community Center (lunch stop, Hemphill KY area; coal-mining mural)
planning_notes: Kentucky dogs are often unleashed (leash ban); previous teams advised air horns. The team bought four horns for eight riders, so buy one per rider.
A dog charged a rider who swerved into bushes; a passing driver stopped to block the dog while the chain was fixed.
Dairy bar about 30 miles past Hemphill serves milkshakes and ice cream.
KY-15 after Hazard has a few miles of unsettling traffic.

summary: Second learning festival at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard KY, with Krispie Koncrete, physics of sound speakers, 3D-printed bubble wands, and strawberry DNA. The afternoon was spent in town at Hazard Coffee Co., the Mother Goose Inn, and the Perry County fair.
slept_at: Bed & Breakfast in Hazard KY
learning_festival: Challenger Learning Center, Hazard KY. Activities: Krispie Koncrete, Physics of Sound (speaker building), 3D printing (bubble wands), strawberry DNA. Center has simulated missions (Lunar Quest, Expedition Mars), microgravity simulator, and mission control mock-up. Festival ran about 3 pm wrap-up.
contacts: Charles (Challenger Learning Center, Hazard KY; organized the festival and gave a center tour)
planning_notes: Challenger Learning Center in Hazard KY is a strong LF venue: staff coordinated the festival and gave a tour afterward.
Hazard in mid-June was about 90s and humid; the fair offered misting and shade. Plan afternoon outings with that in mind.

summary: Hazard KY to Koomer Ridge (70.8 mi, 4,211 ft): dogs chased riders through unleashed-dog Kentucky, mid-90s afternoon heat, and a pothole on a gravel road caused a fall; closed roads forced a 10-mile backroad detour.
slept_at: Koomer Ridge campground, KY (camping)
planning_notes: Kentucky dogs often run loose, and their owners' leash ban is common. Passing slowly and making eye contact usually means the dogs stay put.
Afternoon temperatures were mid-90s with little roadside shade; start early and plan water stops.
Gravel road near Koomer Ridge had a pothole that caused a fall. Gravel sections are slow going.
Route closures near Hazard forced a detour; a parkway or interstate was considered and rejected in favor of 10 extra miles on back roads.
A small-town soda fountain near Hazard gave free Gatorade and Dr Pepper to riders.

summary: Red River Gorge campground to Lexington KY (64.3 mi, 2,702 ft): the team started at 5 am to beat heat, bought distillery tour tickets during a long Dairy Queen stop, and were hosted by Ken and Tricia in Lexington.
slept_at: Ken and Tricia's home, Lexington KY (host)
contacts: Ken and Tricia (hosts, Lexington KY; cooked dinner)
planning_notes: Start around 5 am in Kentucky summer heat so the ride ends before the afternoon heat.
Lexington has distillery tours; the one visited was about 8 miles from the host, and tour tickets can be bought ahead.
Lexington KY terrain flattens out from the Appalachian climbs.

summary: Lexington KY to Liberty KY (69.3 mi): a cafe lunch in Danville, team nicknames, meme-making after arrival at 2 pm, and an overnight at a church in Liberty; one rider got sick from the team's food and cooler.
slept_at: Church in Liberty KY (church host; pastor)
contacts: Pastor of the Liberty KY church hosting the team (name not stated)
planning_notes: The team cooler was not keeping food safe; one rider became ill. Invest in a better cooler and check food temperatures.
Danville KY has a cafe that was a good lunch stop.

summary: Liberty KY to Mammoth Cave National Park (83.08 mi, 3,698 ft): a reroute took riders down a dead-end dirt road and then onto gravel; the team crossed into Central time and took the Discovery Tour at Mammoth Cave with Ranger Brendan.
contacts: Ranger Brendan (Mammoth Cave National Park, Discovery Tour guide)
planning_notes: Routing from Liberty KY to Mammoth Cave included a dead-end dirt road into a backyard and a gravel stretch; check reroutes against a map.
The route crosses from Eastern into Central time in western KY, so the day feels an hour different.
An early start left enough time for the Mammoth Cave Discovery Tour (ranger-led).

summary: Short 32-mile ride from Mammoth Cave to Bowling Green KY after a rider finally got 8+ hours of sleep. The team worked from Spencer's Cafe, toured a music and thrift store, and stayed in a house arranged by the learning-festival partner.
slept_at: House arranged by the Bowling Green learning-festival partner (Accelerate KY)
contacts: Accelerate KY (Bowling Green KY; learning-festival partner that arranged housing)
planning_notes: Spokes free time disappears into maintenance and admin; schedule computer work and route planning for rest days.
Spencer's Cafe in Bowling Green has a park view and works well for team work sessions.
A learning-festival partner arranged a house for the team in Bowling Green, which was a big morale boost after camping and hosts.

summary: Largest learning festival so far at Accelerate KY in Bowling Green (50-60 middle schoolers): physics demos, Krispie Koncrete, strawberry DNA, 3D printing, and speaker building, which got local TV coverage. Several riders then got a stomach bug.
slept_at: House arranged by the Bowling Green learning-festival partner (Accelerate KY)
learning_festival: Accelerate KY, Bowling Green KY, middle schoolers (about 50-60 expected). Activities: 3D printing, Krispie Koncrete, strawberry DNA, Physics of Sound (Chladni plate, speaker building), plus a physics demo intro (tennis racket theorem, bike-wheel gyroscope, Euler's disk). Students rotated through lessons.
contacts: Accelerate KY (Bowling Green KY; partner that hosted the festival and provided photos)
Sam Ford (MIT alum; toured the Accelerate KY facility with the team the day before)
planning_notes: Middle schoolers: keep super glue supervised; several students glued their fingers together during the speaker build.
Tour the partner facility the day before, as the team did with Accelerate KY, to plan crowd size and layout.
Teaching a physics demo at the start of the day kept students engaged while others arrived.

summary: Bowling Green KY to Madisonville KY (85.4 mi, 4,063 ft): a GPS route sent riders onto a gravel forest road that two riders bushwhacked through with bikes, then they jumped a divider to ride the state highway shoulder. Hank's parents supported the team with water and electrolytes.
slept_at: Life Christian Center, Madisonville KY (church host)
contacts: Pastor John and family (Life Christian Center, Madisonville KY; sweet tea and dinner)
Hank's parents (visited from Chicago; brought water, ice, and electrolytes on the ride)
planning_notes: GPS routed the team onto unpaved forest gravel with no clear end on the Bowling Green to Madisonville route; the team stopped and got back on the highway. Check gravel sections before following a GPS route.
A burger bar about 30 miles from Madisonville is a good lunch stop with milkshakes and root beer.
Several roads near Madisonville were closed; plan state highways in advance.

summary: Driver's-day post: Madisonville KY to Harrisburg IL (82.27 mi). A thunderstorm delayed packing and the team camera had to be rescued, a rider's chain was stuck and the bike was driven back after the toolbox was left behind, and the van crossed into Illinois. The driver team hosted with Sherie and Brad.
slept_at: Sherie and Brad's home, Harrisburg IL (hosts)
contacts: Sherie and Brad (hosts, Harrisburg IL; bikepacked across America and shared kombucha)
planning_notes: Driver duties include grocery runs, lunch stops, water-stop prep, and on-call emergency response.
Keep bike tools in the van at all times; a stuck chain could not be fixed roadside because the toolbox was back at the church.
Kroger in Madisonville KY was used for a grocery run for the team (tofurky, bagels, deli meat, cheese, canned meat).
Dogs chased riders in Illinois too, and headwinds made the afternoon slow.

summary: Short 43-mile ride from Harrisburg IL to Gun Creek Campground: the team spent the morning in Benton IL at a coffee shop, an antique shop, and the library, then swam in the lake at Gun Creek and prepared for a 104-degree century ride the next day.
slept_at: Gun Creek Campground, IL (camping, lakeside)
contacts: The Buzz coffee shop, Benton IL (team met many locals here)
Benton IL mayor (former bike shop owner; met the team at The Buzz)
Benton IL public library staff (offered soda, lemonade, and cookies)
planning_notes: Benton IL has a coffee shop (The Buzz) and a library that welcome riders to work on route planning and blogs.
Gun Creek Campground IL is lakeside with swimming; book ahead.
Forecast was about 104 degrees for the next day's century; plan for extreme heat.

summary: Gun Creek Campground IL to St Louis MO (107 mi, 2,180 ft) in 100-plus-degree heat: riders started at 4:30 am, drafted in pairs for the first half, and one rider ran low on water at mile 60 before a homeowner refilled bottles; the team finished the century at 102 degrees and had dinner with an MIT alum.
contacts: Deepa (MIT alum; dinner with the team in St Louis)
Homeowner in rural Illinois who refilled water bottles (name not stated)
planning_notes: On 100-plus-degree days, start before dawn (riders left 4:30-5:45 am) and carry extra water.
Water gaps in rural Illinois cornfields are real: a rider had to wait under a tree at a lonely house with no answer; a passing homeowner refilled bottles.
Drafting within about 2 feet of the rider ahead saves effort; the team rotated lead every 5 miles.
A gas station just outside St Louis was a good water stop.
